SM-1.name: h-junction universality
SM-1.details: 3/5 Xsh compounds have MONITORING primary (ksh, lsh, osh all 100%). But tsh=100% FLOW and psh=100% MARKING. The h-junction is not universal — t and p atoms override it. Needed 4/5.

SM-2.name: Base-dependent category shift
SM-2.details: 4/5 Xs compounds show different primary category than X alone. es: THERMAL->STAGING, os: STAGING->OPERATION, cs: OPERATION->MARKING, ks: THERMAL->STAGING. Only ls stayed STAGING (l-initial already 76% STAGING). Every Xs compound is 100% concentrated in single category.

SM-3.name: PREFIX amplification
SM-3.details: Both test groups pass. a-base: sa purity 52.3% beats ka 42.9% and ta 46.0% (loses to da 56.3%) — 2/3 beaten. h-base: sh purity 30.2% beats ch 25.2% with fewer active categories.

SM-4.name: Suffix distribution modifier effect
SM-4.details: 2/3 pairs significant. Pair 1 (sh-initial vs h-initial): chi2=20.55, p=0.009 — sh-initial 100% bare. Pair 3 (es vs e): chi2=822.25, p<0.001 — dramatic suffix shift. Pair 2 (ksh vs kh): p=0.237, not significant.

SM-5.name: Line position shift
SM-5.details: 1/3 testable pairs significant. sh-initial massive shift (delta=-0.437, p~0) but N=5. kh had zero tokens (INCONCLUSIVE). es and os marginal shifts (~0.088) not reaching significance.

SM-6.name: FQ macro-state amplification
SM-6.details: 1/3 testable pairs. es showed massive STAGING enrichment (+52.5pp). os and cs did not shift. ksh and lsh INCONCLUSIVE (missing base groups). Revised to use CategoryClassifier since s-compounds are mostly HT/UN.

SM-7.name: sh vs ch routing divergence
SM-7.details: chi2=211.2, p~0. Strong C1243 replication: sh routes to k-initial 25.7% vs ch 14.8% (ratio 1.74x, stronger than C1243's 1.33x). sh also more e-enriched (72.6% vs 61.0%), confirming C1203.

SM-8.name: Modifier consistency (DECISIVE)
SM-8.details: Mean cosine 0.966, all 5 testable compounds >= 0.925. ks=0.981, es=0.975, os=0.986, cs=0.962, ls=0.926. s's modifier effect is extremely stable — reproducible and predictable across independent corpus halves.

upgrade_decision: REMAIN PLAUSIBLE — 5/8 modifier battery (enhanced characterization range). Combined 11/20 across both batteries, below 12+ threshold for SOLID. Key finding: SM-8 proves s is a PREDICTABLE base-dependent modifier (cosine 0.966), not random noise. But h-junction non-universality (SM-1) and sparse data (SM-5, SM-6) prevent upgrade.
key_findings: SM-8 DECISIVE: s's modifier behavior is extremely stable (cosine 0.966 across corpus halves) — predictable, not noise
SM-2: s systematically shifts partner category (4/5), with every Xs at 100% single-category purity
SM-1 INFORMATIVE FAIL: h-junction not universal — tsh=FLOW, psh=MARKING. t and p atoms override the sh->MONITORING pathway
SM-3: s-modifier PREFIXes amplify base selectivity (higher purity than other modifiers)
SM-4: s changes suffix selection (sh-initial 100% bare, es dramatic suffix shift)
SM-7: sh routes differently from ch (replicates C1243 at 1.74x ratio, stronger than original 1.33x)
s is a PREDICTABLE BASE-DEPENDENT MODIFIER: it doesn't inject a category, it systematically transforms its partner's category in a reproducible way
characterization_revision: s should be understood as a 'sequencing modifier' — it orders/stages its partner's operation. When combined with h, the result is monitoring (sequenced watching = verification/scanning). When combined with other atoms, the partner's operational domain is preserved but shifted to a new category. The shift pattern is stable (0.966 cosine) and deterministic (100% purity per compound).
